events.description: Gromyko, Andropov, Ustinov, Ponomarev submit report on further measures in Afghanistan.
CC CPSU Politburo session (protocol No. 181) approves the report.
Gromyko, Andropov, Ustinov and Ponomarev submit a report to the CC CPSU on further measures to protect USSR interests regarding Afghanistan.
The CC CPSU Politburo (session, protocol No. 181) approves the Gromyko-Andropov-Ustinov-Ponomarev report and tasks the MFA, Ministry of Defense, KGB and International Department with implementation.
actors: International Department of the CC CPSU

events.description: The April 1978 revolution in Afghanistan, whose goals the USSR pledges to help the PDPA realize.
The government of Babrak Karmal comes to power in the DRA, following Soviet military assistance.

Gromyko, Andropov, Ustinov and Ponomarev sign and submit a report to the CC CPSU proposing measures on Afghanistan, including demoralizing Afghan immigrant organizations, pressuring Zia ul-Haq, and aiding the PDPA.
The CC CPSU Politburo session considers the report on the situation in Afghanistan.
The report anticipates a further activation of the insurgent movement in Afghanistan in spring 1980 and proposes agreements defining the status of Soviet military contingents.
The April 1978 revolution in Afghanistan is cited as the basis for Soviet support to the PDPA leadership.

key_claims: The Soviet leadership claimed US, allies and PRC aimed to use Afghanistan to prolong conflict and tie down the USSR.
The Politburo proposed pressing Zia ul-Haq via special channels to limit rebels operating from Pakistan.
Moscow planned measures to demoralize Afghan exile organizations and discredit their leaders.
The report blamed Hafizullah Amin's criminal activity for anti-Soviet moods.
It recommended negotiations with tribal leaders, work with moderate Muslim clergy, and PDPA unity.
